chapter: Recordings, later jobs and changing times
title: Liking the blues; modern fast tempos and showmanship
summary: Harry loves creating in the blues; he finds current Tiger Rag tempos twice as fast as the old record and ascribes this to showmanship.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: What the word "jazz" means: origins, Dixieland and labels

blocks.x: What about the blues in general? Do you like to make up the blues that way?
I love the blues because you can create as you go along. And of course as you play the blues you're inspired.
I like the blues very much.
Is there anything about the tempo that is to me it seems sometimes they play everything faster. Well to mention one record that you made too I guess you remember the Tiger Rag Stampede. Oh yeah.
Well believe me I was playing with Leverda in New York. Now he plays just about twice that fast. Really? As we recorded it.
Yeah. But in the old age.
Yeah he plays it much faster because I don't know the people seem to like it. Yeah it seems. The public in general.
Maybe they think that's hot stuff when it goes fast. I imagine so. In the old days did they ever play anything fast like that fast?
You can't play anything pretty in that fast tempo can you? No. No. They never played that fast. Just a wild sound.
Well might I say that it's more showmanship than the old days. Yeah I get it. You've got to be a pretty good showman now. And that counts a lot.
